newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa gets closer to multi-year budgeting.
newsitem.headline: South Africa gets closer to multi-year budgeting.

text.p: The South African Finance Ministry has asked all government departments to draft parallel best-case and worst-case three-year budgets as part of its budget reform programme, officials said on Wednesday.
Director General of Housing Billy Cobbett told legislators the exercise was part of the government's broad budget reform programme.
"Every state department at national level is right now writing two three-year budgets.

"One of the three-year budgets is what it would cost to implement our policies and the second budget that we have been asked to write is what would happen to our policies if we froze expenditure at the real level of 1997-98," he said.
"One is a growing budget and one is a standstill budget."

Deputy Minister of Finance Gill Marcus confirmed to Reuters that a letter had been sent to departments asking them to prepare twin scenarios for next year's budget, the first that will be based on multi-year expenditure plans.
"We're asking people to look at their priorities. We're not assuming that there will no increases, but we're saying: If we do freeze funding, what are your priorities.
"And then we're saying: If you got an increase, what would you do given a three-year horizon," she said.

"What we're seeing is that some departments, given a three-year horizon, change their approach and they're quite right. If they know the funding is assured, then they don't need everything on their budget this year," she said.
Marcus stressed that the exercise was part of a broad budget reform initiative to improve the accuracy and efficiency of financial planning.

Finance Minister Trevor Manuel cut government spending in real terms in his March 12 budget and reduced the projected deficit to four percent of gross domestic product from over five percent in fiscal 1996/97.
Manuel's macroeconomic strategy commits the government to reducing the deficit to three percent by the turn of the century.
